study.question: Does a direct, field-separated readout of per-action target evidence recover information that the inherited single normalized history vector fails to expose, and is any gain attributable to target-conditioned volume rather than activity alone? Observed baseline AUCs are static 0.6050036145, pooled 0.6102261137, and din 0.6133619861. The supplied source sums category, brand, action and recency embeddings before a single normalized pooling. Uniform replication of a supplied event multiset therefore leaves its normalized pool unchanged, while it changes per-action evidence counts. This is a source-level information limitation, not an observed failure of a trained attention distribution.
study.hypothesis: Scene-scoped hypothesis, not controlled support: bounded log counts of nonzero encoded category and brand matches for each action will improve full-population validation AUC beyond both normalized match rates and target-independent field-support counts. Baseline-din category_match_present AUC is 0.6107123176 on 2516922 exposures (129821 positive,2387101 negative), versus 0.6176437395 on the 717129 absent exposures (29616 positive,687513 negative). These are different populations and do not establish missing relevance or a causal effect. Existing trajectories are all successful references; no failed or abandoned experimental branches are supplied. Raw tables, causal construction checks and training execution are unavailable in this jail; inherited host receipts and frozen protocol are the reproducible starting evidence, not a fresh reproduction. The static snapshot as-of limitation remains.

nearest_work.source_ref: https://arxiv.org/html/1706.06978v4 ; v4 2018-09-13, section 4.3, Eq.3 and following intensity discussion
nearest_work.difference: DIN already motivates nonnormalized relevance intensity; no priority claim for preserving intensity. Here preserve the inherited normalized learned pool and append eight deterministic action/field counts, with normalization and target-free replacement controls.

This inspected author-code path uses softmax at line 207 despite the paper discussion. Preserve that source conflict: the field-adapted local reference is neither a complete paper reproduction nor evidence that all DIN implementations discard intensity.

nearest_work.source_ref: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.10764v1 ; v1 2023-11-15, sections 3.3.1 Statistical Attributes and 3.4 Target Module; abstract and mechanism sections read
nearest_work.difference: DGIN already uses heterogeneous behavior counts and a candidate-related branch. The proposed local simplification uses only the existing bounded category/brand prefix, with an eight-scalar readout instead of lifelong item groups, group self-attention and Transformer modeling. Category/brand equality is coarser than item identity. This is an adaptation and controlled mechanism question; novelty is unverified.

Author README verifies category, brand and behavior type availability without historical item IDs. No full-paper or DMR architecture reproduction claim; the local readout never substitutes ad IDs for unavailable history item IDs.

nearest_work.source_ref: https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2020/hash/68ce199ec2c5517597ce0a4d89620f55-Abstract.html ; Kalman Filtering Attention, abstract; linked primary PDF opened
nearest_work.difference: KFAtt explicitly warns that frequent behaviors need not be important and introduces frequency capping. This is counterevidence to assuming more count is universally beneficial; the rate cells can outperform the count candidate. No KFAtt reproduction is attempted.

inherited_components: Host data identity, causal histories and first-six-day training split; full validation scorer; no withheld outcomes
baseline-din shared static/history category and brand embeddings, action and recency embeddings, query construction, PReLU attention, softmax mask handling and classifier widths
DIN interest-intensity motivation and DGIN behavior-statistic idea; no claim that either is locally proven
study.proposed_difference: Append eight statistics ordered category then brand, each pv/cart/fav/buy. For count c and action count n, count cell uses log1p(c)/log(129); rate cell uses log1p(128*c/max(n,1))/log(129). The match factor counts nonzero supplied encoded IDs equal to the current ad field; support factor counts nonzero historical IDs without reading the target for this statistic. Both factors leave the learned target-aware attention path identical. Empty action groups give exact zeros. Every cell has eight scalar inputs and identical trainable shapes; no loss or optimizer modifications. Model code has only numeric imports and no I/O. Implementations are standalone candidate.py and three control modules. The proposed difference is from the local reference, not an asserted new general architecture.
predictions: Predeclared primary: match_count exceeds baseline-din and both match_rate and support_count on full validation ROC-AUC. If only one contrast improves, claim only that narrower observation.

Factorial evidence: target conditioning gain AUC(match_count)-AUC(support_count) exceeds AUC(match_rate)-AUC(support_rate). Report this difference descriptively, without treating nonlinear AUC interaction as a causal decomposition.
Secondary unweighted Logloss should not materially deteriorate. If ranking and calibration disagree, report both; select by frozen primary AUC.

Exploratory existing slices: examine category_match_present and past_cart/fav/buy_present, history length and user training frequency, always with host sample/positive/negative counts. Do not infer a mechanism by comparing disjoint slice AUCs. The first-512 diagnostics summarize encoded-match/support counts and action volume only and are not representative population estimates.

Default added capacity is 1024 weights (predicted total 17131299); all four cells match exactly. Extra feature computation is O(B*L*4) with no new sequence attention. Measure wall/GPU seconds, peak memory, throughput and p50/p95 latency; no efficiency claim before host measurements.
falsifiers: match_count fails to improve full validation AUC over baseline-din or the matched controls: this implementation has no supported benefit.
support_count matches or exceeds match_count, or the target-by-scale interaction is nonpositive: target-conditioned volume explanation lacks support even if general activity features help.
match_rate matches or exceeds match_count: preserving absolute volume is unnecessary or harmful in this implementation.
Gains fail to repeat across paired seeds, are confined to a tiny exploratory slice, or come with consequential Logloss/cost regressions: retain preliminary or negative status.

Host checks reveal information-boundary violations, nonfinite outputs or cap breaches: retain failed receipt, treat as execution/integrity failure rather than scientific counterevidence, and do not alter the frozen protocol.
alternative_explanations: Counts describe only the supplied last 128 events, not full lifetime activity; 3026583/3234051 validation exposures are in history_gt64, so truncation may censor volume

The rate intervention removes per-action sample size using a fixed exposure of 128. Log compression and feature distribution also change; equal parameter count does not establish equal optimization difficulty
Encoded equality can reflect hashing or shared unknown codes; only ID zero is excluded. No raw item identity or field encoding guarantees beyond the supplied API are assumed
Category and brand target missingness can affect the match/support contrast; support controls retain history field missingness but do not condition on target availability
This factorial tests target conditioning and count normalization, not the causal value of action stratification versus pooled action counts
Single-seed results and slice comparisons are exploratory; user-frequency priors, label base rates, and action mix may explain gains
All enriched cells beating baseline could reflect direct readout accessibility, 1024 added weights or changed initialization rather than target-conditioned intensity.
Target-match features could exploit exposure-policy or popularity associations rather than stable user interest; this is predictive evidence, not a causal preference claim.

The inherited label-free attention may already encode counts indirectly through recency, action mix and sampled content; source-level replication invariance does not imply large real-data predictive loss.
